note: Eight guards, all cited in a .claude/rules/** Guards block — so a dead one here misleads every future session. Three were already known-broken with the diagnosis done (smoke:orbit permanently red since cycle 7; test:frag:scan recorded as having no assertion; smoke:liquify measured at ~23% false-red in cycle 12). Batches 1-3 lessons applied as a per-guard checklist. The tree was quiet and this auditor's alone; it started the Vite dev server (npm run dev, :3400) — nothing was listening at start.

citedBy: .claude/rules/sibling-apps.md (as a NEGATIVE citation — correct, left alone)
guards.baselineNote: PERMANENTLY RED, reproduced byte-identically from cycle 7: 'accumulation did not advance after orbit settled (1 -> 1)', same sceneOffset delta 4.127, exit 1.
guards.exitContractNote: Throw-based; main().catch -> console.error + process.exit(1). Correct. Stops at the first failed assertion, which is normal (batch-1 lesson 9).
guards.diagnosis: Not a regression and not a code defect — a window two orders of magnitude too small. Headless Chromium falls back to SwiftShader (gpuInfo 'ANGLE (Google, Vulkan 1.3.0 (SwiftShader Device (Subzero) (0x0000C0DE)), SwiftShader driver)'), where one 1200x800 path-trace sample AFTER the gesture settles costs 13.2 / 14.7 / 15.2 / 13.5 / 14.5 / 13.5 s over 6 consecutive clean trials (6/6 advanced, none under 13 s). The poll window was 8000 ms. It is slower post-settle than during boot because the adaptive-resolution grace has expired and the pipeline is back at full res (holdForAdaptive / getAdaptiveGrace in engine-gmt/engine/FractalEngine.ts). The comment defending the 8 s window said accumulation runs at 'a few frames/sec'.
guards.break: Three falsifications, each applied and reverted independently, all run against the REPAIRED guard. (A) engine-gmt/navigation/Navigation.tsx — gated out absorbOrbitPosition's body, so camera.position is never folded into sceneOffset. (B) engine-gmt/engine/FractalEngine.ts — forced holdActive = true, so the accumulation hold never releases after the gesture (the render-loop-stall bug class). (C) engine/RenderPipeline.ts — hard `return` at the top of render(), i.e. the entire accumulation pipeline dead.
guards.result: (A) RED — exit 1, 'orbit drag did not move the scene — sceneOffset delta 0.000 < 0.5'. (B) RED — exit 1, 'accumulation did not advance after orbit settled (1 -> 1) in 45s', full window consumed. (C) GREEN — exit 0, 'accumulation 7 -> 8', advanced in 0.0 s versus ~13 s on a clean tree. That is the finding below.
guards.verdict: permanently-red (repaired) + a measured blind spot on render liveness

guards.note: Strongest of the batch. Three things it does right and that the weaker guards in this batch did not. It DISCOVERS its targets from the live registry rather than hardcoding names, with an explicit `assert(false, 'found a ... param to test')` on each else-branch, so a rename cannot silently turn it into a no-op. It asserts AGREEMENT with the shared compose rather than a hardcoded sum, so it tests the invariant rather than arithmetic. And it carries its own anti-vacuity assertion — `want !== 2.5`, 'and the curve actually bent it' — which is precisely what makes break (B), the exact historical bug, detectable. No change made.

findings.summary: smoke:orbit — cited in three rules and the only browser guard that drives a real camera gesture through Navigation.tsx — had never been green, so it could not distinguish a regression from its own baseline. The cause is a poll window of 8000 ms against a SwiftShader post-settle sample cost of 13.2-15.2 s, measured over 6 consecutive clean trials.
findings.change: Raised the accumulation poll window to a named ACCUM_TIMEOUT_MS = 45_000 (~3x the worst observed) and recorded the measurement, the reason post-settle is slower than boot, and the falsification results in the source header. No assertion was changed, removed or narrowed. The guard now reports the elapsed time on success so the margin stays visible. navigation.md and gmt-features.md dropped their 'currently RED — read the output, not the exit code' warnings and gained the measured caveat instead.
findings.verification: Baseline reproduced byte-identically from cycle 7 (exit 1, 'accumulation did not advance after orbit settled (1 -> 1)', delta 4.127). Latency measured with a throwaway probe driving the smoke's exact sequence: 6/6 trials advanced, 13221 / 14731 / 15249 / 13487 / 14451 / 13478 ms. Repaired guard green, exit 0, 13.5 s. Falsified in both directions AFTER the repair, each break applied and reverted independently: absorbOrbitPosition gated out in Navigation.tsx -> exit 1 on assertion 1; holdActive forced true in FractalEngine.ts -> exit 1 on assertion 2 after consuming the full 45 s. git diff clean, AUDIT_GS01B4 grep empty, typecheck exit 0, check:rule-guards steady at 3 pre-existing issues.

findings.summary: A green smoke:orbit does not prove anything was rendered. `accumulationCount` is not a render counter in app-gmt: whenever progressive tiling is active, engine-gmt/engine/FractalEngine.ts assigns `pipeline.accumulationCount = band.sampleCount` from the band scheduler, OUTSIDE RenderPipeline.render(). A hard `return` at the top of engine/RenderPipeline.ts's render() — the whole accumulation pipeline dead — leaves the smoke exit 0.
findings.rationale: CLAIM: with render() dead, the guard passes with 'accumulation 7 -> 8' and does so in 0.0 s, versus ~13 s on a clean tree — the broken build reads 50x healthier because it does no work. This is batch-1 lesson 1 (a probe flag not meaning what its name says) in the same shape as smoke:engine-gmt's hasCompiledShader, and the pre-drag counter raced to 64 instead of 2. EVIDENCE: the assignment is grep `band.sampleCount` in FractalEngine.ts; RenderPipeline.render()'s own auto-increment is explicitly skipped when `_blendOverride` is set, and its comment says so. No other readable proxy channel discriminates — measured on the same break: frameCount 128 -> 186 (it is the worker's tick count, and gate-skipped frames are the only thing it drops), convergenceValue 1.0 both ways, isBooted and hasCompiledShader true both ways. Only pixels differ: an element screenshot of the render canvas is a 562882-byte PNG on a clean tree and 127196 bytes on the break. OPTIONS: (a) add an additive pixel assertion — screenshot the render canvas element immediately before the drag and again after the settle, and require the two to differ, since a dead pipeline leaves the viewport unchanged while a live one repaints it (the element screenshot clips to the canvas box, so the constantly-updating UI chrome is not captured); (b) assert a MINIMUM elapsed time for the accumulation step — cheap and it directly encodes 'broken renders faster', but it would false-red on a real GPU where a healthy sample is genuinely sub-second, so it is wrong; (c) leave it and rely on the header/rule note now recording the limit. RECOMMENDATION: (a), but NOT unattended and NOT in the same pass as the timeout fix. It is a new assertion on a browser smoke, and cycle 12's smoke:liquify finding is precisely what happens when one of those ships without a measured false-red rate — it would need at least 8 consecutive clean runs at ~25 s each before adoption, and a decision about what to do at high accumulation counts where consecutive samples converge and the pixel delta shrinks toward zero. Not applied: adding an unmeasured assertion to a guard three rules cite is how a guard that was just made trustworthy becomes flaky instead.

Separately, the record that it has no assertion is CONFIRMED: forcing hasDE = false in the V3 detector, so every one of the 200 library formulas is rejected, moved its counts from 2 / 42 / 2 to 156 / 0 / 44 and still exited 0.

findings.summary: test:frag:scan's 'both fail' category — formulas the Formula Workshop cannot open on EITHER import path, which its own output labels 'unrenderable on selection — should be hidden' — has a baseline of exactly two files, and both are deliberate. That makes a real green-baseline gate available where none looked available.
findings.rationale: CLAIM: the two both-fail entries are Claude/Mandelbulb.frag and Claude/Quaternion.frag, and V4 rejects both with kind 'donotrun' — 'marked #donotrun (library file, not a standalone formula)'. They are include-target library files, not formulas the picker is meant to open, so their failure is correct behaviour rather than an importer gap. EVIDENCE: the classifier is grep '#donotrun' in engine-gmt/features/fragmentarium_import/v4/ingest/frag.ts, which emits that error kind; the scan prints both filenames with both error strings. The gate would have caught the falsification break outright — forcing hasDE = false took both-fail from 2 to 44. OPTIONS: (a) skip files V4 classifies 'donotrun' before scoring, which makes the both-fail baseline a natural 0 and lets the script gate `bothFail === 0` with NO allowlist at all — the cleanest form, and it also makes the report match what a Workshop user can actually select; (b) keep scanning them and allowlist the two by NAME, dated in source — works, but batch 2's check:zindex finding is exactly about an allowlist quietly exempting the files that mattered, and this one would grow; (c) gate on a count ceiling (bothFail <= 2) — an allowlist with the names removed, strictly worse than (b); (d) leave it ungated. RECOMMENDATION: (a). It needs one decision I should not make unattended: whether the report is supposed to describe the library as authored or the library as the picker presents it. If #donotrun files are filtered from the Workshop picker then (a) is strictly more accurate as well as gateable; if they are offered, then a user CAN click them and get an error, and the right fix is upstream in the picker rather than in this script. Not applied: it changes what the report measures, and the answer depends on picker behaviour I did not verify.

findings.summary: smoke:liquify measured 3 failures in 13 consecutive runs on an unmodified tree (~23%) at three different assertions, so it could not distinguish a regression from its own noise. Cycle 12 diagnosed it but could not fix it — two other auditors were editing the tree, and there was no way to run enough post-change trials to beat a 23% baseline statistically.
findings.change: Ported both hardening mechanisms from the healthy sibling debug/smoke-gx-geom-handles.mts (13/13 clean in the same measurement): a dep-optimize retry loop around the first page.evaluate, and the dual-instance overlay check, which turns '[1] liquify canvas missing' from a mystery into a message naming the cause and the fix. Replaced the one-shot fixed waits before every readback with polling — wait for the render to CHANGE, then wait for it to SETTLE (two consecutive identical signatures), then assert on the settled value; physics never settles so [4] polls for a live frame instead. Nothing narrowed. .claude/rules/sibling-apps.md's flakiness warning rewritten to match.
findings.verification: 10/10 consecutive clean runs after the change, every one reporting the same 3.77 / 21.03 / 51 as before it — the numbers are unchanged, only the timing discipline is. Falsified with three breaks in gradient-explorer/fullscreen/modes/liquify/, each applied and reverted independently, one per assertion: the push case's offset zeroed in LiquifyMesh.warp -> exit 1 '[2] push brush did not change the render (delta=0.00)'; moveHandle's position write dropped -> exit 1 '[3] grab handle did not change the render (delta=0.00)'; gl.drawElements removed from LiquifyRenderer -> exit 1 '[1] rendered gradient looks blank/uniform (variety=1)'. All reverted, git diff clean on gradient-explorer/, AUDIT_GS01B4 grep empty, typecheck exit 0.
findings.honestLimit: The flake was NOT reproduced on a quiet tree beforehand — 3/3 green before any change — so 10/10 after is evidence the guard is stable, not proof the fix is what made it stable. The likeliest reading, and it is now stated in both the source header and the rule: cycle 12 measured a tree under concurrent editing, and an edit to the store module is exactly what HMR-invalidates it into the dual-instance state whose symptom is '[1] liquify canvas missing', the first of the three observed failures. The rule now says a red run on a QUIET tree is a real liquify regression, not noise. No liquify divergence was found — the CPU and GL paths both behaved identically across 14 runs.

findings.summary: test:modulation-coverage's block [8] — the source scan that catches keyframeable-but-not-modulation-aware vector widgets, a JSX-prop bug no store poking reaches — reads a hardcoded five-file list, and had both of the failure modes an allowlist has. A NEW panel with a keyframeable Vector*Input is simply not scanned and the check stays green having never looked at it. And the scan can SHRINK: renaming only the space-delimited `<Vector3Input ` usages and leaving the newline-delimited ones took it from 10 elements to 3 with every assertion still green.
findings.change: Additive only, original assertion untouched. Added a discovery pass that walks the tree for keyframeable Vector*Input consumers and fails if any file outside the scanned list holds one; a printed element count so coverage is visible in the output; and a recorded floor of 10 replacing the weaker `scanned > 0`, with a message telling the reader which direction to move it and why.
findings.verification: Both new assertions falsified independently. A keyframeable Vector3Input added to components/PerformanceMonitor.tsx (outside the list): green before, exit 1 after, naming that file. The partial rename that used to pass: green before at 3 elements, exit 1 after with 'the Vector*Input scan did not shrink (expected >= 10)'. The move-a-file direction was already safe and was checked rather than assumed — adding a non-existent sixth path throws ENOENT and exits 1. Original coverage confirmed intact post-repair by re-running two earlier breaks: liveValue dropped from a Vector4Input -> exit 1 on the original block-[8] assertion; the lighting-branch break -> exit 1 with the same 3 failures. Clean tree exit 0, scan reports 10 elements across 5 files. All breaks reverted, marker greps empty, typecheck exit 0.

findings.summary: The block-[8] element regex `<Vector[234]Input[\s\S]*?\/>` also matched the TYPE annotation `React.FC<Vector2InputProps>` and then ran on to the first `/>` inside the component body — so it classified components/vector-input/index.tsx, the widget's own definition file, as a consumer. Batch-2 lesson 6 (a text assertion is one spelling away from blind) in its false-positive direction.
findings.change: Tightened to `<Vector[234]Input(?=[\s/>])[\s\S]*?\/>` and recorded at the site why the lookahead is load-bearing.
findings.verification: Found by the discovery pass added in the same commit, which is a fair advertisement for adding one — it reported the definition file as an unscanned consumer on its first run. The scanned element count is unchanged at 10 before and after the tightening, so nothing real was being matched by the loose form; only the discovery walk, which reads files the five-file list does not, was affected. Clean tree exit 0 after.

findings.summary: test:shader reported a clean all-pass sweep with 87% of its matrix missing. Both scripts in the chain derive their case list from registry.getAll(), and the exit code reads only `fail` — a matrix that never ran scores zero failures. Commenting out `import '../engine-gmt/formulas/index.ts'`, the side-effect import that registers every native formula and exactly the sort of line an import reshuffle drops, took the config sweep from 54 formulas to 7 and the weave sweep from 2704 pairs to 49. Both printed all-pass and exited 0. The weave matrix is quadratic in the formula count, so a shrink there is worse than it looks.
findings.change: Additive: a recorded floor on the eligible-formula count in both scripts (54 and 52, today's measured values), checked before any case runs, with a message saying which direction to move it. --formula / --pair / --primary single-case modes are unaffected — the floor is on the registry, not the selected cases. The pre-existing 'Nothing to do (use --fresh)' exit 0 is deliberately left alone: that one is a legitimately-resumed run, not an empty registry. Also recorded in the header what the sweep does NOT compile, measured rather than assumed.
findings.verification: The compile gate was proven live first: a hard GLSL syntax error appended to the `de` block in engine-gmt/engine/ShaderBuilder.ts gives exit 1, 0 pass / 54 fail, every failure on webglCompile. Two earlier breaks were the WRONG breaks and are recorded as such so they are not rediscovered — removing the uCameraPosition declaration, and appending the same syntax error AFTER main, both stayed green, because stripEngineMain deletes from the first `void main(` to the last `}`. That boundary was then measured: for Mandelbulb the Main shader is 106834 chars, the first `void main(` is 98.6% of the way in, and `main` is the only function-like definition at or after it, so positions 1-16 of the assembly order are all compiled. The registry break was run before and after the repair: exit 0 both scripts before, exit 1 both after, each naming the count it got and the count it expected. Clean tree green both ways afterwards. All breaks reverted, typecheck exit 0.

findings.summary: test:partial-apply block [4] — 'empty featureIds opens no transaction' — could not fail. It read `fakeStore._txOpen === false` after the call returned, and applyPartialPreset closes its transaction in a `finally`, so that latch is false whether or not one was ever opened. Deleting the `if (featureIds.length === 0) return;` early exit outright left the entire harness green.
findings.change: Additive: the fake store now COUNTS beginParamTransaction calls, block [4] asserts the count did not move for an empty selection, and an anti-vacuity assertion requires a non-empty selection to move it by exactly one — otherwise the new check would pass because nothing is being counted. The original _txOpen assertion is kept alongside as 'and none left open'; nothing was removed. Three @see citations pointing into `dev/`, the split tree deleted 2026-06-17, were repointed at the surviving paths.
findings.verification: Blocks [1]-[3] and [6] proven live and isolating first: dropping the userScoped/preserveOnApply skip reds [3] alone; dropping the onUpdate==='compile' skip reds [6] alone; dropping the `?? config.default` fallback reds three assertions across [1] and [2]. The empty-featureIds break was run before and after the repair: exit 0 before, exit 1 after with 'no transaction OPENED for empty selection (begins: 4 -> 5)'. Clean tree exit 0 printing 4 -> 4 for the empty selection and 4 -> 5 for a real one. Original coverage confirmed intact post-repair by re-running the preserveOnApply break -> exit 1 on its own assertion. All breaks reverted, git diff clean on engine-gmt/, AUDIT_GS01B4 grep empty, typecheck exit 0.

findings.summary: test:migrations block [7], which covers the ADR-0106 nyquist-fraction-to-Hz conversion, made two claims that could not fail. Every audio fixture started at freqStart: 0, and 0 x 24000 is 0, so replacing `r.lowHz = r.freqStart * LEGACY_NYQUIST_HZ` with `r.lowHz = r.freqStart` — the low half of the conversion gone entirely — left the whole harness green; only freqEnd was ever proven. And the migration's explicit idempotence guard could be deleted outright with the harness still green, because the replay fixture cannot reach it: the first pass deletes freqStart/freqEnd, so on the second pass there is nothing left to re-convert.
findings.change: Two fixtures added, no assertion changed. A 'mids' rule at 0.05-0.25 pins the low half at 1200-6000 Hz. A 'mixed' rule carrying lowHz 300 / highHz 900 alongside freqStart 0.5 / freqEnd 0.9 pins the guard — that mixed-vintage shape is the only one it actually protects.
findings.verification: Both breaks run before and after the repair: the lowHz scale drop was exit 0 before and exit 1 after on the new non-zero-band assertion; the idempotence-guard removal was exit 0 before and exit 1 after on two assertions of the mixed-vintage rule. Original coverage confirmed intact by re-running the v1 break (the `delete q.escape` that reroutes a stray quality.escape) -> exit 1 with the same 2 failures as before. Clean tree exit 0, 24 assertions. All breaks reverted, git diff clean on app-gmt/, AUDIT_GS01B4 grep empty, typecheck exit 0.
findings.sideFinding: Writing the mixed-vintage fixture surfaced a contradiction inside the migration itself, pinned as-is rather than 'fixed': the `continue` that protects an existing Hz band also skips the `delete r.freqStart / r.freqEnd` below it, so a mixed-vintage rule keeps its stale fractions — which contradicts the block's own neighbouring assertion that 'the old fields are removed, not left alongside'. Harmless today: `grep -rn freqStart` across engine, engine-gmt, components, store and app-gmt finds no reader outside the migration. The harness now asserts the ACTUAL behaviour with that reasoning recorded, so any future restructure of the guard is deliberate.

findings.summary: Five of the seven registered scene migrations have no fixture in the only guard that covers migrations, and the rule that cites it calls migrations 'the risk'.
findings.rationale: CLAIM: `listMigrations()` returns 7 entries — v1 escape-radius-to-coloring, v2 engineSettings-to-shaderCompiler, v3 legacy-weave-absorption, v4 faithful-marcher-unification, v5 solid-sky-backdrop, v6 fog-tint-inversion, v7 modulation-band-to-hz. test:migrations exercises v1 and v7. v2-v6 are never invoked with a scene that triggers them, so any of them could be gutted with the guard green. EVIDENCE: the harness's own header enumerates its blocks and they map onto v1 and v7 only; its filename (test-escape-migration.mts) says as much. .claude/rules/scene-and-formula-format.md's Migrations section says 'every field added to a scene has to survive a round-trip from an older file' and 'append to the chain, don't renumber' — neither is mechanically checked. WHAT IS ALREADY TRUE, measured with a throwaway probe so the proposal starts from facts: the chain's versions are contiguous 1-7 with no duplicates, and applyMigrations is idempotent across five representative scenes (bare Mandelbulb, legacy MandelTerrain, stray quality.escape, audio bands, and the real BioCube.gmf) — once-vs-twice deep-equal in every case. Note the probe's FIRST form reported BioCube as non-idempotent and that was a probe defect, not a code defect: it compared JSON strings built with different key orders. OPTIONS: (a) add one fixture per uncovered migration — most coverage, most work, and each needs its own falsification to be worth anything; (b) add two cheap generic assertions instead, both with a green baseline today: version contiguity / no duplicate versions (which mechanically enforces the rule's own 'append, don't renumber'), and chain-wide idempotence over the fixtures already present (the property the harness itself calls load-bearing, since the version tag is not persisted in GMF so a save/reload replays the whole chain); (c) both, (b) first. RECOMMENDATION: (c) — (b) is small, generic and immediately green, and it makes the NEXT untested migration cheaper to catch, while (a) is the only thing that actually covers v2-v6 and is best done one migration at a time by whoever remembers what each was for. Not applied: (a) is five new fixtures whose expected values I would be inferring from the migration code they are meant to check, which is how a test becomes a restatement of the implementation; (b) is defensible unattended but belongs with (a) rather than shipped alone as a proxy for coverage.

summary.headline: Seven of eight needed work, and the worst are all the same shape: a guard that reports a clean pass because its INPUT vanished rather than because the code is sound. test:shader printed all-pass with 87% of its formula matrix missing; test:frag:scan reported a clean library with the library gone; test:modulation-coverage's source scan shrank from 10 elements to 3 and stayed green. Second theme, three instances: a fixture whose value makes its own assertion arithmetic-free — test:migrations proved a Hz conversion with freqStart: 0, where 0 x 24000 is 0 either way. And smoke:orbit, red on pristine main since cycle 7 and never diagnosed, was red for the dullest possible reason: an 8-second poll window against a SwiftShader sample that measurably takes 13-15 seconds.

batchLessonsApplied.probe-flag semantics: Decisive on smoke:orbit. accumulationCount is assigned from the band scheduler OUTSIDE RenderPipeline.render(), so with the whole accumulation pipeline dead the guard passes — and passes 50x FASTER (0.0s vs 13s), the same 'broken reads healthier than baseline' shape as batch 1's hasCompiledShader. frameCount and convergenceValue were checked too and neither discriminates.
batchLessonsApplied.degenerate fixtures: Found the batch's worst assertion-level defect (test:migrations' freqStart: 0) and block [4] of test:partial-apply, whose latch reads false whether or not a transaction opened. Also PREVENTED a false finding: a first idempotence probe reported BioCube.gmf as non-idempotent, and rather than reporting it, the probe was rewritten — it had compared JSON strings built with different key orders. The chain is idempotent across all five scenes.
batchLessonsApplied.a failing break may be the wrong break: Applied twice on test:shader before reporting anything. Removing a uniform declaration and appending a syntax error after main BOTH stayed green; rather than declaring the compile gate dead, the break was moved into the DE block, where it goes red 54/54. The boundary was then measured (98.6% of the shader is compiled) and recorded so the next auditor does not repeat it. Same discipline on test:partial-apply block [5], which is loose rather than dead.
batchLessonsApplied.allowlists exempt what matters: test:modulation-coverage's five-file scan list, in both directions — a new consumer is never scanned, and the scan can shrink. The discovery pass added to close it immediately found a third thing, the loose element regex matching `React.FC<Vector2InputProps>`.
batchLessonsApplied.green with zero coverage is still green: The dominant finding of the batch — three separate guards, all repaired with a recorded floor rather than an allowlist.

Left rather than deleted (Tier C: never delete a file), same convention as batch 3's leftover. Bin them by hand if you want the tree tidy.

summary.finalState: All eight green on a clean tree at the end of the run, exit 0 each: smoke:orbit 25s (13.5s of it the accumulation step), test:frag:scan 30s (200 frags, counts 2 / 42 / 2), smoke:liquify 22s (3.77 / 21.03 / 51), test:modulation-coverage 12s (443 targets, 10 scanned elements), test:shader ~14min run to completion (54/54 x3 then 2704/2704, CHAIN_EXIT=0), test:partial-apply 8s, test:modulated-setter 8s, test:migrations 8s (24 assertions). typecheck exit 0. Every falsification break reverted; `grep -rn AUDIT_GS01B4|VecRenamedGS01B4|MOVED_AUDIT` across engine, engine-gmt, components, store, utils, hooks, app-gmt, demo, fluid-toy, fractal-toy, gradient-explorer, mesh-export, palette and .claude returns nothing. git status shows only the untracked debug/engine-gmt-smoke.png and this result file.
summary.processNote: One self-inflicted mistake worth recording: on test:shader a break was reverted with `git checkout -- <file>` on a file that also held my uncommitted repair, which wiped both. The repair was re-applied and re-verified, and nothing was lost — but on a file carrying uncommitted work, revert a break with a targeted Edit, not a checkout. This is the same class as PROTOCOL.md's staging warning: a broad git operation in a tree with work in flight.
